title: Daytime selection kept ozone contrast signs but removed 44 percent of two contrasts in North Wales in August-September 2021
abstract: We tested time-window sensitivity of achieved ozone differences in a public wildflower warming experiment. August and September 2021 supplied 1,464 complete hourly records. A fixed 08:00-19:59 window kept all four nonzero signs of heated-minus-ambient accumulated ozone above 40 ppb. It removed 44.7% and 44.2% of two contrasts while removing only 1.64% and 0.75% of their ambient exposure sums and none of the heated sums. An exact partition explains this sensitivity through near cancellation. Three ozone thresholds and four selection rules kept all nonzero contrast signs, but magnitudes varied. One site, one year, one dome per treatment, uncertain clock metadata and unmarked source filling limit inference. This exposure audit does not test flower responses or stomatal uptake. Original code, aggregate results, source hashes, independent numerical checks and a figure are included. Source records remain external.
